managePayments.heading: Payments
managePayments.state.not_connected.title: Not set up
managePayments.state.not_connected.body: It takes about 10 minutes. You need your bank details and your ID.
managePayments.state.requirements.title: Stripe wants your details
managePayments.state.requirements.body: Card payment will not work until Stripe gets your business and bank details.
managePayments.state.pending.title: Connected — Stripe is checking your details
managePayments.state.pending.body: You do not need to do anything. Stripe is reviewing what you sent; when they finish, this page updates.
managePayments.state.ready.title: Connected
managePayments.state.ready.body: Your Stripe account is connected and can also take payments.
managePayments.state.restricted.title: Card payment temporarily stopped
managePayments.state.restricted.body: Stripe has temporarily stopped card payment on your account until an issue is resolved.
managePayments.state.unsupported.title: Card payment is not available on this account
managePayments.state.unsupported.body: Stripe cannot enable card payment here. Contact us; we will solve it together with you.
managePayments.keyMismatch.title: The Stripe keys do not match
managePayments.keyMismatch.body: This website’s server uses the {server, select, live {live} other {test}} Stripe key; but the browser was built with the {browser, select, live {live} other {test}} key. At the moment a customer tries to pay, the card payment will fail; so setting up Stripe is blocked until the two agree.
managePayments.keyMismatch.fix: Both keys must be set for the same kind of environment; after that the website must be rebuilt — the public key is included at build time; the secret key is read on every request.
managePayments.permission.title: Only the food truck’s owner can set up payments
managePayments.permission.body: Stripe is connected by the person whose bank account receives the money; so it must be set up from their own account that they are logged into. There is no problem with this food truck or with HatchGrab.
managePayments.config.keyMissingTitle: Card payment is not set up yet
managePayments.config.fetchTitle: We could not check this food truck’s Stripe account
managePayments.config.keyMissing: {name} is not set — the embedded components cannot load.
managePayments.online.heading: Online payment
managePayments.online.body: Customers pay by card when they order. The money goes directly into your own Stripe account — we never hold it.
managePayments.online.feeLine: Stripe charges {fee} for each payment on standard {region}. Other cards may cost more. HatchGrab’s own fee on online orders is decided by your plan — see “Billing”.
managePayments.online.testMode: Test mode. Real payments cannot be taken yet.
managePayments.trialNote: Setting this up does not start your subscription, and it charges you nothing today. This is the way your customers pay you — your plan is a separate matter.
managePayments.admin.title: Viewing as the platform admin
managePayments.admin.body: This food truck has not set up online payment. Only the owner can start it, from their own logged-in account — there is nothing to press here.
managePayments.toast.addDetails: Now enter your details for Stripe
managePayments.onboarding.restricted: From here Stripe takes over — you sign in to Stripe and update the details needed.
managePayments.onboarding.firstRun: From here Stripe takes over — you sign in to Stripe and give your business and bank details.
managePayments.details.title: Your Stripe details
managePayments.details.body: Change the bank account the money goes into, or update your business details and documents.
managePayments.walkUp.heading: Payment for walk-up orders
managePayments.walkUp.body: How you take money at the truck. Whichever you choose, HatchGrab charges no platform fee on walk-up orders.
managePayments.walkUp.ownTerminalHelp: Zettle, Square or whatever you use now. Nothing to set up — only your provider’s own fees apply.
managePayments.walkUp.hatchgrabHelp: Uses the same Stripe connection as your online payment — a card machine (POS), or contactless payment you take directly from your phone or tablet.
managePayments.walkUp.hatchgrabFees: {fee} for each payment ({region}); in addition {surcharge} for contactless payment you take on a phone or tablet. Other cards may cost more.
manageCharges.heading: Tax, tips and service fees
manageCharges.rate.label: Sales tax rate
manageCharges.rate.hint: The rate you charge on every order. Customers see it added when they pay, on the receipt and on the order ticket.
manageCharges.rate.regionDefault: If you leave it empty, {label} will be {rate}% — this is the rate charged on food prepared and sold ({region}).
manageCharges.included.label: {label} is included in your prices
manageCharges.included.hint: Your prices already include {label}. This rate only shows how much of each price is {label}, on the receipt and order ticket — nothing is added when paying.
manageCharges.included.default: If you leave it empty, {rate}% is used — this is the rate charged on hot food sold to take away (tax: {label}, {country}).
manageCharges.tips.label: Tip
manageCharges.tips.hint: Customers paying online by card can add a tip. It all reaches you.
manageCharges.fee.label: Online service fee
manageCharges.fee.hint: Added on online orders only. Never added on “Pay at the truck” orders or walk-up orders. The money is yours.
manageCharges.fee.example: Customers see it before they pay, in one line: “{label} {amount}”.
manageCharges.fee.hatchgrab: HatchGrab adds a {fee} service fee to your customers’ online orders. You do not pay it, and you cannot change it.
manageCharges.saveFailed: Could not save — please try again.
takingPayment.heading: Taking payment
takingPayment.intro: How your team records money for each order.
takingPayment.paidStepHelp: Adds a button saying “Confirm” when you add an order yourself; so you can enter the order now and take payment later. If you take phone or advance orders, switch this on.
takingPayment.paidStepNote: This only concerns orders you add. It does not affect online orders.

manageWhatsApp.preview.title: Try it before you connect
manageWhatsApp.preview.intro: Write the kind of question a customer would ask; see exactly what answer they would get. Nothing is sent to anyone.
manageWhatsApp.preview.placeholder: What kind of desserts do you have?
manageWhatsApp.preview.noReplyWhy: That reads as spam, a booking request or something unrelated; so the WhatsApp auto-reply stays silent.
manageWhatsApp.preview.footnote: The replies are generated by artificial intelligence; they differ slightly each time; and occasionally they can be wrong.

manageWhatsApp.notice.setupFailed: The setup could not be completed. Nothing was changed.
manageWhatsApp.notice.metaError: Meta reported a problem during setup. Nothing was changed. Try again; if the problem continues, contact us.

manageWhatsApp.card.title: WhatsApp auto-reply
manageWhatsApp.card.description: Answers customer questions automatically on your social media, using your menu and schedule.
manageWhatsApp.card.requiresAccount: A WhatsApp Business account is needed.
manageWhatsApp.card.popupInstruction: A Facebook window will open to connect your WhatsApp Business account. If nothing shows, allow pop-up windows for hatchgrab.com in your browser; then press “Set up” again.
manageWhatsApp.card.switchedOff: WhatsApp auto-reply is switched off for your food truck.
manageWhatsApp.card.expiring: Your WhatsApp connection must be renewed soon. So the WhatsApp auto-reply continues, press “Reconnect”.
manageWhatsApp.card.instagram: Auto-reply to Instagram direct messages. Needs an Instagram professional account.
manageWhatsApp.card.messenger: Auto-reply to Facebook Messenger. Needs a Facebook Page.
manageWhatsApp.blocked.title: Your replies are not arriving
manageWhatsApp.blocked.body: Because of a billing problem on your WhatsApp Business account, WhatsApp has refused to send your automatic replies. Customers can still message you, and you still see everything they send — but they are not getting a reply.
manageWhatsApp.blocked.fix: You pay WhatsApp directly for these messages; so this is fixed in WhatsApp Manager. <link>Check your payment method</link>
manageWhatsApp.limit.heading: WhatsApp auto-reply
manageWhatsApp.limit.label: Monthly limit
manageWhatsApp.limit.perCustomer: Up to {n} replies per customer within 24 hours; then one message saying you will reply personally.
manageWhatsApp.limit.emailAt: When you reach your limit, replies pause. We will email you when you reach 80% and 100%.
manageWhatsApp.billing.heading: Billing
manageWhatsApp.billing.summary: It is Meta, not HatchGrab, that bills your WhatsApp account for the replies. Starting from this date: {from}, the first {free, number} replies a month are free. Date checked: {checked}; for changes see <link>Meta’s prices</link>.
manageWhatsApp.billing.chargesTitle: It is Meta, not HatchGrab, that charges for WhatsApp replies.
manageWhatsApp.billing.chargesBody: Meta charges your WhatsApp Business account for each reply HatchGrab sends for you. Starting from this date: {from}, Meta includes {free, number} free replies a month per number; after that each reply is charged at Meta’s price. Replies you send yourself from the WhatsApp Business app are not charged. Meta decides these prices, and may change them. <link>See Meta’s prices</link>
manageWhatsApp.billing.addPaymentInManag: Add a payment method in WhatsApp Manager
manageWhatsApp.billing.aboveMissing: Your limit is above Meta’s free replies ({free, number}). Without a payment method, Meta stops all replies once those are used up.
manageWhatsApp.billing.aboveGeneral: Your limit is above Meta’s free replies ({free, number}). Replies beyond that need a payment method on your WhatsApp account; without a payment method, Meta stops all replies once the free ones are used up.
manageWhatsApp.disconnect.title: Disconnect WhatsApp?
manageWhatsApp.disconnect.body: The WhatsApp auto-reply stops immediately; HatchGrab loses its access to your WhatsApp account. Your number keeps working in the WhatsApp Business app. To remove HatchGrab completely, also open this: WhatsApp Business → Settings → Account → Business Platform.
manageWhatsApp.signup.partial: We linked your WhatsApp Business account, but we could not complete the connection. Nothing is wrong on your side — please contact us; we will finish it.
manageWhatsApp.signup.noNumber: Your WhatsApp Business account is linked, but no phone number came back. Press “Reconnect” and complete the number step.
manageWhatsApp.signup.needsRegistering: Your account is linked, but before replies start this number must be registered by us. Please contact support — your setup is saved; don’t run it again.
manageWhatsApp.signup.registerRefused: Your account is linked, but Meta was not willing to register the number. Your setup is saved — instead of running it again, please contact support.
manageWhatsApp.signup.deliveryRefused: Your account is linked, but Meta was not willing to switch on message delivery. Your setup is saved — instead of running it again, please contact support.
manageWhatsApp.signup.numberTaken: That WhatsApp number is already connected to another HatchGrab account. A number can answer for only one food truck. Contact support; we will move it.
manageWhatsApp.signup.saveIncomplete: We are nearly done — we could not finish saving. Your setup is saved; instead of running it again, please contact support.
manageWhatsApp.signup.connected: WhatsApp is connected. The WhatsApp auto-reply will start answering messages that come to this number.

customDomain.apex.too_deep: That address has too many parts. Something like events.{domain} works better.
customDomain.record.guide: The provider’s own guide to this ({provider})
customDomain.record.addSomewhere: Add this where your web address is managed, and save.
customDomain.record.hintWord: Only this word, not the whole address.
customDomain.record.timing: It usually starts working within an hour, but it can take longer. You do not need to keep this page open.
customDomain.record.someoneElse: Is your web address managed by someone else?
customDomain.providers.cloudflare.open: Open your web address; then “DNS” and “Records”.
customDomain.providers.cloudflare.name: Enter the first value below in “Name”.
customDomain.providers.cloudflare.value: Enter the second value below in “Target”.
customDomain.providers.cloudflare.proxy: Make “Proxy status” “DNS only” — the cloud beside it must be grey, not orange.
customDomain.providers.cloudflare.caveat: If the cloud stays orange the padlock sign will never appear; and nothing will explain why.
customDomain.providers.godaddy.open: Open “Domain Portfolio” and choose your web address.
customDomain.providers.godaddy.add: Select “Add New Record”; then in the “Type” menu choose “CNAME”.
customDomain.providers.godaddy.name: Enter the first value below in “Name”.
customDomain.providers.godaddy.value: Enter the second value below in “Value”.
customDomain.providers.godaddy.save: Leave “TTL” as it is and select “Save”.
customDomain.providers.godaddy.caveat: If you added more than one record at a time, the button says “Save All Records”.
customDomain.providers.123reg.signIn: Sign in to the “123 Reg Control Panel”.
customDomain.providers.123reg.manage: Beside “Domains”, select “Manage All”; then choose your web address.
customDomain.providers.123reg.name: Enter the first value below in “Name”.
customDomain.providers.123reg.value: Enter the second value below in “Value”; and add a dot (.) at its end.
customDomain.providers.123reg.caveat: 123 Reg needs a dot (.) at the end of the second value; otherwise it will not work.
customDomain.providers.wix.open: Open “Domains”; then press the “Domain Actions” icon beside your web address.
customDomain.providers.wix.add: In the “CNAME (Aliases)” section press “+ Add Record”; then press “Got it”.
customDomain.providers.wix.name: Enter the first value below in “Host Name”.
customDomain.providers.wix.value: Enter the second value below in “Value”.
customDomain.providers.wix.save: Press “Save”; then press “Save Changes” in the pop-up window.
customDomain.providers.wix.caveat: If your web address only points at Wix rather than being held by Wix, Wix cannot make this change — whoever holds the address must do it.
customDomain.instructionsEmail.subject: Schedule page: {truckName} — one record to add
customDomain.instructionsEmail.introAt: We are putting the food truck {truckName}’s live schedule on this address: {address}; for this, one record must be added on our domain (provider: {provider}).
customDomain.instructionsEmail.introHold: We are putting the food truck {truckName}’s live schedule on this address: {address}; for this, one record must be added on our domain, through whoever holds our domain.
customDomain.instructionsEmail.wholeChan: This is the whole change — nothing else on the website is affected; and the rest of our domain keeps working exactly as it does now. It usually starts working within an hour.
customDomain.instructionsEmail.pointsAt: The page it points to shows where we sell next; and it updates itself.
customDomain.instructionsEmail.replyTo: If you have questions, reply to this address: {email}.
customDomain.liveEmail.subject: {address} is working
customDomain.liveEmail.body: Your schedule is now showing at your own address. Look at it and check it is right: open {address}; check the events are yours and the dates are right.
customDomain.liveEmail.confirm: After you have done this, open your settings on HatchGrab and tell us it is right. Nothing depends on that — it is only so we know a person has seen it.
